title: Put a foam insole back in a laced sneaker: bend it through the opening, push it home to the hidden toe, seat it flat
instruction: Put the blue insole into the sneaker so that it lies flat on the bottom of the shoe, pushed all the way in to the toe with its heel end down inside the heel, then let go of it and the shoe. You may hold the shoe and move its tongue; leave the laces tied.
context: People take the insoles out of their sneakers to wash, dry or replace them, then put them back with the shoe still laced. A full-length insole is about twice as long as the collar opening, so it goes in toe first, bent down behind the tongue, and slides along the bottom under the laced front, out of sight. The tongue leans back over the opening and has to be held forward out of the way. A hand cannot follow into the toe box, so the insole is pushed home from its heel end. Whether its toe has reached the end of the toe box cannot be seen: it shows only in the part still in view, when the heel end drops down behind the heel counter into the heel cup and the insole lies flat. Held flat, the insole bridges the opening and never goes in; pushed too little, its toe stops short and its heel stays up on the counter. The hard part is bending a soft sheet longer than its opening, guiding it blind and pushing it home from the far end while the other hand holds the tongue aside.
setup: A wooden table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart; positions are forward of the line between the bases and leftward (+) or rightward (-) of their midpoint), the station's top camera and a camera on each wrist. (1) A Brooks Ghost 18 men's running shoe, US 9, medium width, any colourway (modelled: charcoal mesh upper, white midsole, black outsole), an everyday lace-up trainer with a removable sockliner; its own insole taken out; laced through its six eyelet pairs and tied in a bow at a marked lacing, about 0.27 kg. As modelled from its published numbers: inside length 271 mm; heel and forefoot stack 36 and 26 mm (10 mm drop), so the bed under the insole is 31 mm above the table at the heel and 21 mm at the ball, with a heel cup whose sides rise 8 mm and a toe spring that lifts the bed 7 mm at the toe; toe box 31 mm high inside; collar opening 130 mm long from the heel counter to the top eyelets; heel counter 65 mm, collar 50 mm high at the ankle; laced vamp 58 mm above the bed at the top eyelets; a non-gusseted 9 mm padded tongue, sewn in under the laces, whose free part (50 x 52 mm) stands up from the top eyelets and leans back over the front of the opening, about 30 degrees from upright. The shoe stands loose, sole down, toe away from the robot, the inside of its heel counter at 33 cm forward, its centre line 3 cm left; tape ticks on the table at its heel and toe. (2) Its cardboard shoe box with the lid on, 30 x 19 x 12 cm, 0.3 kg, long side forward, centred 55 cm forward, 17 cm right. (3) On the lid, top cover up, toe away from the robot, along the box's centre line: a Spenco PolySorb Walker/Runner replacement insole (Cat. No. 38-385, size 3 = US men's 8/9, polyurethane foam with a fabric top cover, 7.5 mm thick at the heel and 6.8 mm at the forefoot), trimmed to the shoe's own insole: 267 mm long, 40 mm wide at the heel end, 66 mm at the heel, 60 mm at the arch, 92 mm at the ball, about 40 g. Its heel end overhangs the lid's near edge by 4 cm (heel tip at 36 cm forward, 17 cm right), so it can be pinched through its thickness. Pen marks on its top along the centre line: a line 20 mm from the toe tip, dots at 30, 100 and 185 mm from the heel end (heel, arch, ball), a line 150 mm from the toe tip. The insole is about twice as long as the collar opening, so it cannot be laid in flat. Its bending stiffness in the simulation is a named parameter that has not been measured: foam modulus 4 MPa, bending stiffness about 8e-3 N m^2; build/ gives a 5-minute cantilever test that measures it on the real insole. The robot may hold the shoe and move its tongue; the laces stay tied as found. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Before trials, measure the shoe and the insole as listed in build/README.md.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial. 0 if the shoe is not standing upright on its sole on the table (tilted more than 10 degrees, on its side, or held up), or if either gripper is within 3 cm of the shoe (with its tongue) or the insole (video), or if at any time during the trial the robot unties or loosens the laces (whole-trial video: the bow comes undone, a lace end is pulled, or a lace leaves its eyelet). Otherwise: 0.25 if the insole is inside the shoe: within its walls, no part of it is higher than the top edge of the collar (a ruler laid across the collar from side to side does not touch it), it is not folded back on itself, and its pen line 20 mm from the toe tip is under the laced vamp, forward of the top eyelets (it cannot be seen looking straight down into the opening with the tongue held forward). 0.5 if in addition it is home: its heel edge is down on the bed (no more than 5 mm above it, not up on the counter) and within 6 mm of the heel counter's lining (steel ruler on the centre line; the trimmed insole is 4 mm shorter than the inside), and its toe is within 10 mm of the end of the toe box (its line 150 mm from the toe tip is at least 111 mm, the inside length minus 160 mm, from the heel counter, measured with the ruler along the bed). 1.0 if in addition it lies flat: pressed lightly straight down with a pencil's eraser end on its heel, arch and ball dots (the ball dot is reached through the opening under the vamp), it moves down by no more than 3 mm at each, read against a ruler held upright beside the pencil. In the simulation the laces are tied and fixed, so they cannot be undone. The simulation measures the same conditions after every control step from the insole and shoe poses (flat: the insole's underside within 3 mm of the bed at the three dots); the trial ends once 1.0 has held for 4 s. Doing nothing scores 0.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX 240 Hz, 20 Hz control, fingers capped at 40 N. Insole: 18 rigid foam slices with constant bending, twist and in-plane springs from one unmeasured modulus (4 MPa); no lateral curl or foam compression. Shoe: one free rigid body of boxes with the published inside length, stack, drop and toe box height; the upper is rigid and, above the arch, up to 15 mm per side wider inside than the insole; laces drawn on a rigid vamp. Tongue: 4 padded slices on soft springs.
reset_notes: Pull the insole out of the shoe by its heel end, lay it top up on the shoe box lid at its marks (heel end 4 cm over the near edge, toe away from the robot), put the shoe and the box back on their tape marks, check the bow is at its lacing marks and push the tongue back so it leans over the opening. About 1 minute; nothing is used up.
